title: Learning estimates mortality after femoral neck fracture
summary: Machine-learning models estimated 90-day and two-year mortality in 2,478 operated patients aged 65 or older with femoral neck fractures. In an internal 495-person test set, selected models achieved concordance of about 0.74 and 0.70, respectively. Model selection on test performance and preprocessing can make these estimates optimistic; the study did not demonstrate improved treatment decisions or survival.
organization: Amsterdam University Medical Centers; Harvard Medical School; Erasmus University Medical Center; University Medical Centre Groningen

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Retrospective 80:20 patient split with measured 90-day and two-year mortality; training cross-validation and internal calibration assessment.
evidence.unknown: Independent frozen-model evaluation and clinical benefit remain unestablished; only operated patients were included, and final model selection used internal test performance.
evidence.ai_role: Supervised boosting and penalized regression learn mortality associations from recorded preoperative clinical characteristics.
